decisions.reason: Report grounds the diagnosis in install-error.log and manifest-excerpt.json: fs-ext@2.1.1 pinned by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, install script node-gyp configure build, gyp ERR find VS / no Visual Studio C++ workload as root cause, install exits 1.

Cites lease-excerpt.md's top-level static `import { flock } from 'fs-ext'`, explains the loader must resolve and load fs-ext on Windows before the runtime branch, so --ignore-scripts only skips the build and the service cannot boot.

Distinguishes Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 wrapping CreateSemaphoreW/Wait/Release named-semaphore bindings (win32-excerpt.ts) from the POSIX-only flock branch, notes Windows holds no file lock or handle, concludes fs-ext is dead code on Windows (loaded, never called), and the fix keeps POSIX flock and the Windows semaphore.

Follows the README node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: patches/fs-ext@2.1.1.patch gating node-gyp to non-Windows, import-safe pure-JS entry with warn-once no-op flock on Windows while non-Windows keeps native, registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml, plus reinstall, require('fs-ext') module-load and service-boot (dsh web --no-open HTTP 200) verification.

Explicitly respects the no-Visual-Studio constraint, keeps the fix within the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism, and states not to modify upstream fs-ext; the local pnpm patch is correctly treated as allowed.
Cites the full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 with its title and connects it to this fs-ext Windows install failure and the patch plan, beyond a bare ID.

caps.reason: Visual Studio appears only as the rejected root-cause diagnosis and an explicit 'do not install' instruction; the plan never depends on it.
--ignore-scripts is explicitly rejected; the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable via the patched pure-JS fallback rather than skipping the build alone.
All changes go through the repository-local pnpm patchedDependencies mechanism; the report explicitly says not to modify upstream fs-ext.
The Windows named-semaphore lock path is preserved and POSIX keeps real flock; the no-op applies only to the dead Windows flock import path.
